title: Promption for Prompt Injection Detection under Source Shift and Three State Enforcement
abstract: Prompt injection defenses must balance malicious-input detection with the preservation of legitimate requests. We present an empirical study of Promption, a reusable software framework combining regular expressions, a lightweight text classifier, and a three-state enforcement policy. A code audit establishes the behavior of the deployed configuration and identifies a positional-index error in the existing data splitter. New experiments use 5872 normalized, unique prompts from five upstream collections, three stratified random holdouts, and five leave-one-source-out evaluations. All vectorizers and classifiers are fitted exclusively on each training partition. On the seed-42 random holdout, strict OR enforcement obtains 83.90% recall with 9.98% false positives, whereas the implemented three-state policy obtains 83.33% recall with 8.11% false positives and routes 89 malicious inputs to output inspection. Source-held-out results reveal substantial variation that random holdouts obscure. The study contributes a reproducible policy comparison and a distinction between input escape, guarded routing, and demonstrated downstream compromise. No language-model attack success or monetary savings are inferred from these classifier experiments. The results support Promption as a measurable input-screening framework while exposing the evidence needed to validate its complete security pipeline.
keywords: Prompt injection, text classification, source shift, security middleware, software evaluation
